newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ monetary conditions weaken sharply before data.
newsitem.headline: NZ monetary conditions weaken sharply before data.

text.p: New Zealand's Monetary Conditions Index fell to more than 100 basis points, in interest rate terms, easier than the level preferred by the central bank on Tuesday morning, ahead of key jobs data due at 2245 GMT.
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand has said it wants to see the MCI index within 50 basis points of 825 during the September quarter, but at 9.00 a.m. (2100 GMT) it dropped under 725.
The index reflects the combined levels of the kiwi dollar's Trade Weighted Index and the prevailing market rate on 90-day bank bills. They stood at 64.30 and 8.28 percent respectively at 9.05 a.m..
Later this morning Statistics New Zealand is due to produce its June quarter Household Labour Force Survey, expected to provide an insight into economic growth trends.
A number of private economists have said they believe the numbers will be sufficiently weaker than Reserve Bank forecasts to justify an easier level of monetary conditions.

According to them, the central bank will respond to the data by moving to sanction a level of conditions as much as 100 basis points easier than its current centre point, which is intended to cover the entire September quarter.
Others disagree, however, saying the RBNZ, which has resolutely stood by its position on monetary policy since it placed the current settings in late June, will not move yet.

In the period before the data release, traders said the most obvious driver of the MCI's fall was that 90-day bill rates had not risen to compensate for a renewed dip in the kiwi dollar that has taken place since Monday.
During Monday the 90-day bills rallied with the rate falling to 8.30 percent from 8.42 percent at the opening, and consolidated these gains early on Tuesday.
At the same time the kiwi has been pummelled lower from about 0.6440 towards 0.6420 against the U.S. dollar and the TWI has eased to 64.27 from 64.58.
